q: Consider the amending procedures: 1-Creation or abolition of a Legislative Council requires a simple majority. 2-Alteration of State boundaries requires a simple majority. 3-Both are counted as constitutional amendments. Which is/are correct?
expl: Neither is counted as an amendment under the amending article.
why: Several important changes are made by simple majority and are expressly excluded from the amendment count.
trapnote: Simple-majority changes are outside the amending article and are not counted as amendments.

q: Which of the following requires ratification by not less than half the State legislatures?
options: Any change to the chapter on Fundamental Rights
Any change to the Directive Principles of State Policy
Any change to a List in the Seventh Schedule
Any change to the Preamble of the Constitution
expl: Distribution of legislative powers is a federal provision requiring ratification.
why: Fundamental Rights need only a special majority, which is the pairing most often mistaken.
trapnote: Federal provisions need ratification. Rights and Directives need only a special majority.

q: Consider the 2023 amendment on reservation of seats for women: 1-It covers the lower House of Parliament. 2-It covers State Legislative Assemblies. 3-It covers the upper House of Parliament. Which is/are correct?
expl: Indirectly elected Houses are outside the amendment.
why: The amendment operates on directly elected Houses only, which excludes the upper House and State Councils.
trapnote: Directly elected Houses only. The upper House and State Councils are outside it.

q: On the commencement of the 2023 reservation amendment, which statement is correct?
options: It operates from the date it received the assent of the President
It operates after the first census conducted after its commencement and the ensuing delimitation
It operates after the first census, delimitation not being a precondition
It operates after a delimitation exercise, a census not being a precondition
expl: Both a census and the delimitation that follows it are preconditions.
why: Two options give one of the two conditions, so partial knowledge produces a near miss.
trapnote: Two cumulative conditions: the census first, then the delimitation that follows it.

q: Consider the 1976 amendment: 1-It inserted three words in the Preamble. 2-It added Fundamental Duties. 3-It reduced the term of the lower House to five years. Which is/are correct?
expl: It extended the term to six years; the reduction came in 1978.
why: The 1976 amendment expanded and the 1978 amendment corrected, which is the pattern to hold.
trapnote: One amendment expanded, the next corrected. Attribute each change to the right one.

q: Consider the 1978 amendment: 1-It substituted armed rebellion for internal disturbance. 2-It placed two articles beyond suspension. 3-It removed property from the chapter on Fundamental Rights. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three limbs belong to the same amendment.
why: The 1978 amendment is best learned as a package of corrections to the preceding one.
trapnote: Three corrections in one amendment: the ground, the protected articles, and property.

q: Which amendment gave constitutional status to the commission for backward classes?
expl: The 102nd inserted the provision constituting that commission.
why: All four numbers are adjacent and all four amendments are real, so recognition alone will not separate them.
trapnote: Adjacent numbers: 102nd commission, 103rd economic quota, 104th seats, 105th State power.

q: Consider the 2021 amendment: 1-It restored the power of States to identify backward classes. 2-It responded to a judicial interpretation of an earlier amendment. 3-It abolished the central list of backward classes. Which is/are correct?
expl: The central list continues; the State lists were restored.
why: The amendment restored a power without displacing the central list, which the third statement denies.
trapnote: Restoration of a State power, not abolition of the central list. Both lists now coexist.

q: Consider the Ninth Schedule: 1-It was created by the first amendment. 2-Laws placed in it are protected from challenge on rights grounds. 3-Laws placed in it after April 1973 may be challenged for damaging the basic structure. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three are accurate.
why: The cut-off date is the date of the decision that established the basic structure doctrine.
trapnote: The Schedule is not an absolute shield. The cut-off is the date of the 1973 decision.

q: On the 2016 amendment relating to the goods and services tax, which statement is correct?
options: It inserted a Council alone, the taxing power arising under the existing Lists
It inserted a concurrent taxing power alone, the Council being created by statute
It inserted a concurrent taxing power, a provision on inter-State supply and a Council
It transferred the entire subject to the Union List with effect from that date
expl: Three provisions were inserted: the taxing power, inter-State supply and the Council.
why: Most summaries mention only the Council, which is why the taxing power is the tested limb.
trapnote: Three provisions, not one. The taxing power is the charging provision; the Council is the body.

q: Consider the 2020 amendment: 1-It extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes. 2-It discontinued nominated Anglo-Indian seats. 3-It reduced the maximum strength of the lower House to 550. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three follow from the same amendment.
why: The reduction in the ceiling is a consequence of discontinuing the nominated seats rather than a separate change.
trapnote: Two express changes and one arithmetical consequence, all from one amendment.

q: On the amendment relating to cooperative societies, which statement is correct?
options: It inserted a Fundamental Right to form cooperative societies alone
It inserted a Directive Principle and extended the freedom of association
It inserted a Directive Principle alone, the freedom being unaffected
It transferred cooperative societies to the Union List
expl: The amendment worked on Part III and Part IV together.
why: The amendment added words to the existing freedom rather than creating a new right, which the second option overstates.
trapnote: One amendment touching two Parts: a new directive and an extended existing freedom.

q: Consider the 2002 amendment: 1-It inserted a fundamental right to education. 2-It reworded a Directive Principle. 3-It added a Fundamental Duty. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three limbs belong to the same amendment.
why: It is the only amendment that worked on Parts III, IV and IVA simultaneously.
trapnote: Three Parts touched at once. That is what makes this amendment distinctive.

q: Which statement about the assent of the President to a Constitution Amendment Bill is correct?
options: Assent is discretionary, the President retaining a power to withhold it
Assent is obligatory, the position having been settled by amendment in 1976
Assent is obligatory, the position having been settled by amendment in 1971
Assent is discretionary, though the Bill may be returned only once
expl: The 1971 amendment made assent obligatory.
why: The third option gives the right rule with the wrong year, which requires both halves to be known.
trapnote: Obligatory assent, settled in 1971 by the same amendment that excluded amendments from the bar.

q: Consider the 1985 amendment: 1-It added a Schedule dealing with disqualification on defection. 2-It provided an exception for a split in a party. 3-The split exception was later removed. Which is/are correct?
expl: All three are accurate; the split exception was deleted in 2003.
why: The deletion of the split defence is the change most often omitted from summaries of the anti-defection scheme.
trapnote: The split defence existed and was deleted. Only a merger now operates as a defence.

q: On the 2019 amendment providing reservation for economically weaker sections, which statement is correct?
options: It inserted an enabling provision in the employment article alone
It inserted enabling provisions in both the education and employment articles
It inserted an enabling provision in the education article alone
It inserted a Directive Principle requiring such reservation to be made
expl: Two enabling provisions were inserted, one in each article.
why: The paired insertion mirrors the structure of the existing backward-class provisions.
trapnote: Enabling provisions come in pairs here: one for education, one for employment.

q: Consider the amending power: 1-Parliament may amend any part of the Constitution. 2-It may not damage the basic structure. 3-A joint sitting may be summoned if the Houses disagree. Which is/are correct?
expl: There is no joint sitting for a Constitution Amendment Bill.
why: The absence of a joint sitting means each House must pass the Bill separately by the required majority.
trapnote: No joint sitting for Money Bills or Amendment Bills. Each House must clear it independently.

q: Which statement about the 1971 amendment is correct?
options: It declared that fundamental rights may not be amended in any circumstances
It declared that amendments are subject to the basic structure doctrine
It declared that an amendment is not law for the purposes of the bar on abridging rights
It inserted the Ninth Schedule to protect laws from challenge
expl: It took amendments outside the definition of law for that purpose.
why: The third option attributes a judicial doctrine to a parliamentary amendment, which is a category error.
trapnote: Parliament removed one check; a court later supplied a different one. Do not merge the two.

q: Consider the special provisions for Andhra Pradesh: 1-They were inserted by an amendment of 1973. 2-They provide for local cadres in public employment. 3-They ceased to apply on the bifurcation of the State in 2014. Which is/are correct?
expl: They continue to apply to both successor States.
why: The provisions survived bifurcation and remain the legal basis of zone-wise recruitment in the State.
trapnote: The 1973 provisions survived the 2014 bifurcation and apply to both successor States.

q: On the special provisions for Andhra Pradesh, which statement is correct?
options: They empower Parliament to prescribe residence qualifications for State posts
They empower the President to provide for local cadres and local-area recruitment
They empower the State government to reserve posts for residents of the State
They empower the Governor to allot candidates to zones after recruitment
expl: The power is exercised by the President through an order.
why: The second option describes a different provision under which the power belongs to Parliament.
trapnote: One provision: Parliament by law. The other: the President by order. Different actors.
